visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: Harbour's adjusted EBITDA is €140m, its reported EBITDA is €100m, and the sector trades at 10x. How much price do the adjustments add?
questions.explain: €40m of adjustments at ten times is €400m of price. €1.4bn is the whole value on adjusted EBITDA, not what the adjustments add.
questions.explain_at: Forty million of adjustments is four hundred million of price

questions.q: Who usually gives an audit opinion on a company's adjusted EBITDA?
questions.explain: The audit opinion covers the financial statements, and adjusted figures usually sit outside them. Regulators ask for a definition and a reconciliation, and a quality of earnings report isn't an audit.
questions.explain_at: The auditor's opinion covers the financial statements

questions.q: A company has booked restructuring costs in each of the last four years. How do you treat them?

options.text: Add them back as a one-off
Keep them as a recurring cost

questions.explain: A cost that comes every year is a cost of running the business, whatever it's called, so diligence reverses the add-back.
questions.explain_at: A cost that comes every year is a cost of running the business

questions.q: Evos has an enterprise value of €2.56bn, an equity value of €1.18bn, revenue of €392m and EBITDA of €219m. What's the EBITDA multiple?
questions.explain: EBITDA belongs to lenders and shareholders together, so divide enterprise value by it: €2.56bn ÷ €219m ≈ 11.7x. Equity value over EBITDA gives 5.4x and mixes two claims.
questions.explain_at: which is the multiple in Adani's statement

questions.q: The board has approved €15m of cost savings that haven't been made yet. What do you do with them?

options.text: Add them back, as the board approved them
Add back half of them now
Leave them out of today's EBITDA
Add them back once they're announced

questions.explain: Approved isn't achieved. If the savings are real the buyer gets them, does the work, and decides how much of them to pay for.
questions.explain_at: Approved isn't achieved. Those fifteen million
